intent.requirement: Add a focused symbol-extraction slice for Rust, mirroring the existing regex-based Go extractor.
author_decisions: extract_rust_symbols(path) in src/agentpack/analysis/symbols.py extracts: free functions (fn, including pub/pub(crate), async fn, const fn, unsafe fn, extern "C" fn), impl/trait methods qualified by their owning type (Type.method), and type constructs (kind="class") — struct (named, tuple, and unit), enum, and trait.
A running brace-depth container stack attributes methods correctly, so impl Trait for Type assigns methods to the concrete Type, and both declared and defaulted trait methods are owned by the trait.
The language-neutral brace helper _go_symbol_end_line was renamed to _brace_block_end_line and shared with the Rust extractor. Go behavior is unchanged.
A small _rust_symbol_end_line helper returns single-line ends for body-less declarations (unit/tuple structs, ;-terminated trait method signatures) and brace-scans everything else.
rust added to the extract_symbols dispatcher (so naming_signals picks it up automatically).
New _rust_summary in src/agentpack/summaries/offline.py (uses the existing rust_imports extractor), plus a rust branch in summarize.
Additive change: no behavior change to existing languages. Rollback = revert the commit.

change_units.what_changed: Added _rust_symbol_end_line helper and extract_rust_symbols function. _rust_symbol_end_line returns start_line for body-less declarations (no '{' AND ends with ';'), else delegates to _brace_block_end_line. extract_rust_symbols iterates lines, maintains a depth counter and a containers stack of (owner_type, brace_depth_at_open). At each line: pops exhausted containers (depth <= their opening depth), determines owner. Matches fn first (creates Symbol with kind=method if owner else function), then impl (pushes to containers but creates no Symbol), then struct/enum/trait (creates kind=class Symbol; trait additionally pushes to containers). Depth is updated at end of each iteration with line.count('{') - line.count('}').

from agentpack.analysis.symbols import extract_python_symbols, extract_js_symbols, extract_go_symbols, extract_rust_symbols
from agentpack.analysis.rust_imports import extract_imports as rust_imports

def summarize(...):
    ...
    if language == "rust":
        return _rust_summary(path, abs_path, file_hash)
    return _generic_summary(path, abs_path, language, file_hash)

def _rust_summary(path: str, abs_path: Path, file_hash: str) -> FileSummary:
    text = _read_sample(abs_path)
    imports = rust_imports(abs_path, text=text)
    symbols = extract_rust_symbols(abs_path)
    intel = extract_code_intelligence(path=path, language="rust", text=text, symbols=symbols)
    effects = extract_side_effects(path=path, language="rust", text=text, imports=imports)
    role_info = infer_role_domain(path=path, language="rust", symbols=symbols, imports=imports, text=text,
        entrypoints=intel.entrypoints, external_systems=effects.external_systems)
    role = role_info.role or _infer_responsibility(path, intel.defines)
    failure_hints = extract_failure_hints(text)
    public_api = _dedupe([*_infer_public_api(path, intel.defines, text), *intel.entrypoints])[:12]
    test_hints = _infer_test_hints(path, role, intel.defines)
    return FileSummary(path=path, hash=file_hash, language="rust", provider="offline",
        schema_version=SUMMARY_SCHEMA_VERSION, ...)

open_questions.question: Does the container pop condition `depth <= containers[-1][1]` correctly handle the case where depth transiently goes negative (e.g. unbalanced braces in string literals or comments in Rust source)? The brace counter uses raw line.count('{') - line.count('}') without filtering strings or comments.
open_questions.matters_because: Macro invocations, string literals, and doc comments containing braces could cause depth to undercount or overcount, leading to premature container pops and incorrect method attribution. The author acknowledges regex-based limits in docs/limitations.md.

open_questions.question: Does _RUST_FN match on lines that are comments or string literals (e.g. a doc comment containing 'fn foo')? The regex matches against stripped line text without filtering for '//' or '#' prefixes.
open_questions.matters_because: A line like '// pub fn example() could appear in Rust source and would be stripped to 'pub fn example()...' — however stripping removes leading whitespace not comment markers, so '// pub fn' stripped is still '// pub fn' which does NOT match _RUST_FN (starts with //). For lines that are NOT commented (no // prefix), the regex is safe.
